_about: Reforma Ortografica de 1911 — the LEXICAL residue that the deterministic rules (ph->f, th->t, rh->r, y->i, k/w removal: see rules.py Reform1911) cannot handle. These are: (a) geminate-consonant reductions whose outcome is not predictable by rule (ll, nn, mm, pp, tt, bb, gg, dd -> single, but rr/ss are kept), (b) ch=/k/ -> c or qu (depends on the following vowel AND on the /k/ pronunciation, which a string cannot know), and (c) etymological silent consonants and medial h that were dropped. Stored as pre-1911 (etymological) -> 1911 (post-reform) pairs.
_sources: Reforma Ortografica de 1911 (Portaria de 1 de Setembro de 1911), comissao de Goncalves Viana

digraph_accented._comment: Digraph words whose modern form also carries a graphic accent introduced by the 1911 systematic accentuation — the bare ph->f/th->t rule cannot supply the accent, so they are listed.

_note: Examples like 'affecto->afecto' show the 1911 target still kept the (then-pronounced or PT-conventional) etymological consonant; the AO1990 drop (afecto->afeto) is a SEPARATE, later edge handled elsewhere. Keep the eras distinct.
